verification.heading: Verification pass — September 2026
verification.markdown:
Checked 2026-09-15 by verification agent. Laws cited as of Sep 2026.
- Ch. 43-07 exam vs bond-only: CORRECTED — neither. § 43-07-04 requires a sworn statement of experience and qualifications, a certificate of liability insurance, and a WSI coverage statement; "examination" appears nowhere in the chapter; § 43-07-11 (contractor's bond) repealed by S.L. 1995, ch. 397, § 9; no financial statement required by § 43-07-04. Old text claimed a financial statement + $2,000–$10,000 surety bond. — https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t43c07.pdf ; https://www.sos.nd.gov/business/licensing-registration/contractors — GOV
- Bond subsections 43-07-11/-12: CORRECTED — § 43-07-11 is repealed; § 43-07-12 is "Bids to show license," not a bond section. — https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t43c07.pdf — GOV
- License threshold/classes (load-bearing a): CORRECTED — trigger is a job that "exceeds" $4,000 (old: "$4,000 or more"); Class D cap is $100,000 (old: $200,000); C $300,000, B $500,000, A unlimited (§ 43-07-07); unlicensed work = class A misdemeanor (§ 43-07-02); renewal before March 2 per § 43-07-10, SOS says on or before March 1. — https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t43c07.pdf ; SOS contractors page — GOV
- Seller disclosure § 47-10-02.1 (load-bearing b): RESOLVED in part — statute applies when a broker/broker associate/salesperson represents or assists a party, 1–4-unit residential, disclosure before the parties sign final acceptance; lists latent defects, general condition, environmental, structural and mechanical categories; no chimney/fireplace item named in the statute. REALTORS form line wording STILL OPEN. — https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t47c10.pdf — GOV
- Ch. 51-15 remedies: RESOLVED — § 51-15-09: up to 3x actual damages if knowing, mandatory costs + reasonable attorney's fees; § 51-15-11: civil penalty up to $5,000 per violation (also for ch. 51-18). — https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t51c15.pdf — GOV
- Ch. 51-18 cancel right: RESOLVED — § 51-18-02(1): 3rd business day; buyers 65+ on purchases over $50: 15th business day. — https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t51c18.pdf — GOV
- CO law (load-bearing c): RESOLVED — N.D.A.C. 24.1-06-01-40 requires CO alarms in dwelling units with fuel-fired appliances or attached garages (outside sleeping areas, every habitable level, interconnected); no point-of-sale requirement. No standalone Century Code CO statute located. — https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/north-dakota/N-D-A-C-24.1-06-01-40 — REF mirror of admin code (not re-read on ndlegis.gov)

No 2025 session change to ch. 43-07 found (SB 2395 created a separate universal-licensure chapter). — https://www.commerce.nd.gov/community-services/building-codes ; https://ndlegis.gov/assembly/69-2025/regular/bill-overview/bo2395.html — GOV

sections.rawHeading: 1 · Licensing (GOV — high confidence; a real state credential, but a money-gate not a skill-gate)
sections.title: State licensing and registration
sections.confidenceNote: high confidence; a real state credential, but a money-gate not a skill-gate
sections.markdown: North Dakota is the rare cold-belt state with a **statewide contractor license** — but it is a **registration keyed to project dollars, not a trade-competency exam.** Under **N.D.C.C. § 43-07-02**, a person may not act as a contractor "when the cost, value, or price per job **exceeds** the sum of four thousand dollars" without a **contractor's license issued by the Secretary of State** (STATE LAW); unlicensed contracting is a **class A misdemeanor** (§ 43-07-02). The license comes in **four classes by maximum single-project value (§ 43-07-07): Class D (up to $100,000), Class C (up to $300,000), Class B (up to $500,000), Class A (no limit)** — chimney rebuild, reline, or a solid-fuel appliance install over $4,000 falls squarely inside this. To get it, an applicant files (§ 43-07-04) **an application under oath with a statement of experience and qualifications, a certificate of liability insurance, and a Workforce Safety & Insurance coverage statement.** **There is no surety bond** — the former contractor's-bond section, § 43-07-11, was repealed by S.L. 1995, ch. 397, § 9 — and **no examination**: the word does not appear anywhere in ch. 43-07, and the Secretary of State's contractor page lists no exam or bond. Application fees run $100 (Class D) to $450 (Class A). Renewed annually on or before March 1 (§ 43-07-10). Public lookup: **firststop.sos.nd.gov/search/contractor**. A **routine chimney sweep of $4,000 or less needs no state license at all** — sweeping and small repair fall below the money-gate; only larger repair/rebuild work triggers it.

sections.title: What the credential does not test
sections.markdown: Wide, and unusually explicit here. The ND license attests **that you carry liability insurance and workers'-comp coverage and filed a sworn experience statement — not that you can diagnose a flue.** Chapter 43-07 contains **no competency exam and no bond requirement** (verified on the ndlegis statute text, Sep 2026). The license is a dollar-class credential, so individual certs (CSIA CCS, C-DET; NCSG CCP/CCR) remain the only real competence signal, and any job of $4,000 or less is entirely uncredentialed.

sections.rawHeading: 3 · Home sale (GOV — medium-high; broker-triggered, chimney not a named line)
sections.title: Seller disclosure when a home sells
sections.confidenceNote: medium-high; broker-triggered, chimney not a named line
sections.markdown: North Dakota's seller disclosure lives in **N.D.C.C. § 47-10-02.1** but is **narrower than most: the mandatory-form duty is triggered when a real estate broker/salesperson represents or assists a party** to the sale of a 1–4-unit residential dwelling — a true **FSBO with no agent can fall outside the form requirement** (STATE LAW). The seller must disclose known material defects across structural, mechanical, heating, and environmental systems on an **actual-knowledge, good-faith** basis; **fireplace/heating condition is captured in the mechanical/heating items, but "chimney" is not called out as its own named line** on the standard ND Realtors form (confirm the exact wording before publish). Disclosure is also **before final acceptance and "except as otherwise provided in the offer to purchase"** — so it can be modified by agreement. No inspection is mandated at transfer; NFPA 211 Level 2 stays a NATIONAL STANDARD.

sections.title: Consumer remedies and cancellation rights
sections.markdown: Two instruments. **(1) The Unlawful Sales or Advertising Practices Act — N.D.C.C. ch. 51-15** — bars any "deceptive act or practice, fraud, false pretense, false promise, or misrepresentation" in a sale; enforced by the **Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division**, with a private right of action under **§ 51-15-09**: if the defendant acted knowingly, the court may award **up to three times actual damages** and **must** award costs and actual reasonable attorney's fees; the AG may also seek a civil penalty of **up to $5,000 per violation** (§ 51-15-11, which also covers ch. 51-18 violations). **(2) Home-solicitation sales — N.D.C.C. ch. 51-18** — give a **3-business-day right to cancel** a door-to-door sale, and notably **15 business days for buyers 65 or older** on purchases over $50, the exact fact pattern of a chimney door-knock scare-sale. Complaints: attorneygeneral.nd.gov.

sections.rawHeading: 5 · Permits & codes (GOV — high on code, medium on local reach)
sections.title: Permits and building codes
sections.confidenceNote: high on code, medium on local reach
sections.markdown: The **North Dakota State Building Code was updated to the 2024 IBC, IRC, IMC and IFGC (plus 2024 IECC and IEBC), adopted Sept. 11, 2025 and effective Jan 1, 2026** (NATIONAL STANDARD via state adoption; replaces the 2023 code based on the 2021 I-codes). Local adoption is optional, but a jurisdiction that elects to enforce a building code must adopt the State Building Code (it may amend it). **IRC Chapter 10 governs chimneys and fireplaces.** Chimney relines, rebuilds, crowns, and solid-fuel appliance installs are generally permit work where a building department exists. The catch is reach: **many rural ND counties have no local code enforcement, so a permit may simply not exist there** — municipalities enforce and may amend the state code locally (LOCAL). Fargo, Bismarck, and Grand Forks run active building departments; unincorporated areas often do not.

sections.rawHeading: 6 · CO law (GOV — medium-high; code-based, not a standalone statute)
sections.title: Carbon monoxide and smoke alarm law
sections.confidenceNote: medium-high; code-based, not a standalone statute
sections.markdown: North Dakota's CO-alarm requirement is **code-based, not a freestanding statute** — it flows from the **adopted IRC (2024 edition from Jan 1, 2026) and the State Fire Marshal rule N.D.A.C. 24.1-06-01-40**, which requires CO alarms in dwelling units with **fuel-fired appliances or an attached garage** — outside each sleeping area, on every habitable level, and in any bedroom containing a fuel-fired appliance, interconnected where more than one is required (STATE RULE + NATIONAL STANDARD via code adoption). There is **no statewide mandatory pre-sale CO certificate.** A permitted chimney or stove job is the natural moment to verify alarms.

sections.title: Solid fuel and environmental rules
sections.markdown: No statewide burn-ban or wood-stove emission regime. Very high wood/pellet heat in a severe-cold plains climate, but no ND-specific stove rule — not a material content section.

sections.rawHeading: 8 · Scam landscape (REF — partial; pull specifics before publish)
sections.title: Scam patterns and enforcement
sections.markdown: The AG's Consumer Protection Division pursues home-repair and door-to-door abuses, and the ch. 51-18 elder 15-day window signals ND's specific concern with senior-targeted door-knock sales — the textbook "we noticed your chimney" pitch. **Specific ND chimney-sweep enforcement actions: NOT CONFIRMED — re-run search before publish.**

sections.title: Season calendar
sections.markdown: Severe cold, long heating season statewide (among the coldest in the launch/expansion set). Burn season ~Oct–Apr. Rush: SEP–NOV. Best booking: MAY–JUL.

sections.title: Price seeding (internal)
sections.markdown: Thin, spread-out market; Fargo and Bismarck metros anchor labor cost, rural travel surcharges are real. Regionalize modestly around the two metros; expect trip fees outside them.

story.heading: The story
story.markdown: North Dakota is a **cold-belt outlier that partly BREAKS the master correlation.** It has a genuine statewide contractor license — but the "license" is a **dollar-threshold insurance-and-paperwork credential — no exam, no bond**, and on the *other* axis its seller disclosure is comparatively **weak: broker-triggered, opt-outable in the offer, and without a named "chimney" line.** So ND lands as a state with a real (if shallow) credential AND a soft disclosure — the same "strong-license / weak-disclosure" pairing the correlation predicts, which is why I read it as CONFIRMING rather than breaking. The oddity worth the page: the $4,000 gate means **a chimney sweep or small repair is completely unlicensed here, while a rebuild is licensed** — the licensing line runs straight through the trade.

faq.q: What should I check before hiring a chimney company in North Dakota?
faq.a: State licensing: YES — state contractor license by dollar class (N.D.C.C. ch. 43-07), required when a job exceeds $4,000; jobs of $4,000 or less unlicensed; no exam, no bond. Registration or credential: SoS contractor license (liability insurance + WSI coverage + sworn experience statement; Classes A–D). Seller disclosure at sale: YES but broker-triggered (§ 47-10-02.1), fireplace within mechanical/heating, "chimney" not a named line. Right to cancel a sale made at your home: YES (ch. 51-18; 15 days for 65+). Carbon monoxide alarm law: code/rule-based (2024 IRC eff. Jan 1, 2026 / N.D.A.C. 24.1-06-01-40); no pre-sale certificate. Where to check a contractor: firststop.sos.nd.gov/search/contractor. Then ask the eight questions below, get the inspection findings in writing with photos, and never sign for "emergency" work on the day of a door-knock.
